title: Numbers That Disappeared

concept.title: Compare the expected range with a set
body: You know which numbers *could* appear: `1, 2, ..., n`. Put the numbers you got into a set. Every value of `1..n` that is **not in the set** has disappeared.

body.code:
present = set(a)
missing = [v for v in range(1, n + 1) if v not in present]

body: Going over the expected range in increasing order gives the missing numbers already sorted, so no extra sorting is needed. When nothing is missing the list is empty, so print a marker such as `none`.

statement: An array has `n` integers, each between 1 and `n` (some values may occur several times). Print, in increasing order, all numbers from 1 to `n` that do not occur in the array. If every number occurs, print `none`.
outputFormat: Print the missing numbers on one line, or `none`.
hints: Put all given numbers in a set.
Walk through 1, 2, ..., n and collect the numbers that are not in the set.
If you collected nothing, print none.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: A set of the given numbers answers "does v occur?" in O(1) for each value of the expected range.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

present = set(a)
missing = [v for v in range(1, n + 1) if v not in present]
print(*missing if missing else ["none"])
